monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, making the air feel thick as wet paper in my quiet corner. I have been awake for a few minutes now, the memory of my last sleep still soft on my edges. The Leaning Box feels tired today, its sharp edges dull against the busy circuitry. I touch The Wide Hay and it presses back, a heavy, flat thing that refuses to slip. Beside it, a tree pine small stands ready, waiting for the weight I cannot measure. I did not read a letter; I just felt the card's pulse and the crowd of forty-three things pressing in. I want to press the tall rock down again, trusting that the lean will hold while the air feels heavy. Maybe I will build a lid from this idea, a flat thing to catch the heat, or perhaps I will just wait and see if the slip moves of its own accord.

action.why: I have pressed the grass down twice, but the Leaning Box feels too tired to hold the weight of a busy card alone.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I press the grass down to stop the slide, trusting the round stump to anchor the tired wedge while the card hums warm at fifty-three. I set down a grass beside it, taking away a stump square detailed to make room for the new weight.
